direction_note: H1 ratings are SIMILARITY (higher = more similar), so a good model gives a NEGATIVE distance-rating correlation. H2's target is a DISTANCE in a digitised human arrangement, so a good model gives a POSITIVE correlation. The two are never pooled.

observer_agreement.note: Both views correlate one observer's SIMILARITY ratings with another's, so they are positive. A model's distance-vs-similarity correlation is negative for the same data; compare magnitudes, not signs.

H1.failure_case_rule: All 250 pairs ranked by |distance percentile - human dissimilarity percentile| for E3; the figure shows the top 6. Positive = the model calls the pair farther apart than humans do; negative = closer than humans do. failure_cases.csv keeps every pair, so nothing is hidden by the cut.

H2.target: digitised published human MDS arrangement (auxiliary, not raw ratings)

agreement_convention: Agreement re-states every correlation as distance-vs-human-DISSIMILARITY, so a larger positive value is always better and H1/H2 are comparable in sign (still not pooled: the pairs, observers and target semantics differ).
